subtitle: Quran revision, on schedule
promotionalText: Meet Revo, your revision coach: ask how your week went, what to revise first, or how anything works. Plus 76 translations and memorizing ayah by ayah.
description:
Revisely is a Quran revision tracker built around a schedule that fits your hifz.

Pick how much you want to cover each day, and Revisely rotates through everything you've memorized on a repeating cycle. As you memorize more, ayah by ayah, the cycle grows with you. Miss a day and the schedule keeps moving instead of piling up, and when you're back, jump to any juz, surah or page.

Inside:

• Three ways to schedule: pages per day (1–60), juz per day (1–5), or a custom plan you build day by day, starting from any point
• Revision page by page: swipe through your pages, check each one off, and optionally rate a page's strength from 1 to 5
• A timer and a recorder on the page: time your sitting, record your recitation and listen back as the pages turn. Each sitting is saved to your day with its ayahs and minutes, and recordings are backed up to your account
• Revo, an AI assistant you can turn on: ask how your week went, which juz to revise first, or how anything in the app works, and get short answers from your own progress, some with a chart. Answers come from Claude, made by Anthropic. Revo can make mistakes, and it's off until you turn it on
• Activity: a calendar of every day you revised, memorized and read, each day with its sessions and your notes. Insights shows the juz you haven't revised lately, your pace and, with Smart Tracking, your weak spots
• Memorize ayah by ayah: log exactly where you stopped, even mid-page. A partly memorized page joins your revision for the ayahs you know
• 76 translations in 56 languages from QuranEnc.com, Saheeh International among them, plus The Clear Quran® by Dr. Mustafa Khattab. Hold any ayah to read one, and download translations to read offline
• Recitation: play an ayah, a page, a surah or a juz with your choice of reciter, speed, repeats and a pause to recite it back. It carries on with the app in the background
• Prayer times and the Qibla, worked out on your phone
• Widgets for your Home Screen and Lock Screen: today's revision, the next prayer, the Qibla and a verse of the day
• Fajr-aligned days: start your revision day at dawn instead of midnight, so a late-night session counts for the right day
• The whole mushaf on your phone for revision offline, in the 1405 or the Madani 1441 print
• Streaks, full session history with editing, daily reminders, and light and dark themes

How it works:

1. Mark what you've already memorized
2. Choose how much to revise each day, and whether your day starts at fajr or midnight
3. Open the app each day, tap Start revision, and swipe through your pages

Sign in with Apple, Google or email, and your progress syncs across your devices. You can delete your account and all of its data at any time from Settings.

Built for people who want to keep the Qur'an they've memorized. Made to be used every day.
reviewNotes:
Revisely is a Quran revision tracker. It is free, with no in-app purchases.

The demo account is pre-populated so you land on a full dashboard: about 166 pages memorized (Al-Fatiha and the last six juz), some of Al-Baqarah in progress, and seven days of completed revision sessions ending yesterday, with Smart Tracking turned on.

New since 1.0.3 (version 1.0.4):
- Revo, an optional AI assistant: the round R button at the bottom right of Home opens it. The first time, it explains what it is and that answers come from Claude, by Anthropic, and asks the user to turn it on (Settings > Revo AI turns it off again). It answers questions about the user's own revision and how the app works, from the account's own data, sometimes with a chart, and can make mistakes. 20 questions a day.
- Search the Qur'an from the Read tab: typed (a surah, 2:255, a page or Arabic words), or by voice on iPhone with the microphone beside the search field. The first voice search downloads a 57 MB speech model once; recognition runs on the device and nothing is recorded or sent.
- 76 translations in 56 languages from QuranEnc.com (licensed), alongside Saheeh International and The Clear Quran®: hold a verse > Translation, then ⋯ > Select translation. They can be downloaded to read offline.
- Activity (the icon at the top right of Home) is a calendar of every day, with Insights beside it (Overview / Insights).
- Memorized pages can be logged ayah by ayah.
- Home and Lock Screen widgets: Today, Verse of the day, Qibla and Prayer times (long-press the Home Screen > + > Revisely).

Once signed in:
- Home shows today's revision. Tap "Start revision": the page fills the screen; tap it for the controls. Swiping past a page marks it revised (or tap the check at the top); ⋯ > Rate page strength rates it 1 to 5. Submit appears once every page is done, or swipe past the last page to finish.
- The bottom bar has two icon tabs: Home and Read (a separate Qur'an reader, with search).
- The icons at the top right of Home open the Prayer sheet, Activity and Settings.
- In a session or the Read tab, the bottom bar holds Play, the reciter, Audio Options, the microphone (records the user reciting; View opens it in Activity) and the timer.
- Recitation (hold a verse > Play, or Play in the bar) continues with the app in the background or the phone locked, with Now Playing controls on the Lock Screen and a mini player in the app; this is what the audio background mode is for.
- Hold a verse > Translation: Saheeh International, or The Clear Quran® by Dr. Mustafa Khattab (⋯ > Select translation), from the publisher's API (Al-Furqaan Foundation) under their developer agreement.
- Settings > Support > Report a problem sends a short report (optionally a screenshot) to our error monitoring service.

Permissions:
- Microphone: only when the user taps record, or the microphone in the Read tab's search (voice search runs on the device and nothing is kept or sent). Recordings stay on the device and are backed up to the user's own account (Wi-Fi only unless mobile data is allowed; Settings > Activity > Back up recordings turns it off). Only that account can read them; deleting a recording deletes its backup.
- Location: only when the user opens prayer times or the Qibla (used on the device only, never sent), or turns on Start day at fajr in Settings > Prayer (then saved to the account to calculate local fajr).
- Notifications: the daily revision reminder, the end of a timed session, and prayer notifications if the user turns them on.

Account deletion: Settings > Delete account (at the bottom) permanently deletes the account and all of its data, including backed-up recordings (guideline 5.1.1(v)).

Qur'an page images: the Madani Mushaf rendered with the King Fahd Complex fonts (open-source quran.com-images), served from our own storage.
